relationships.description: The document's path map gathers path items that may also be defined independently, such as reusable entries in components/pathItems pulled in by $ref, into the set of endpoints the API exposes.
relationships.evidence: A key under the document's 'paths' object holds a $ref pointing to a PathItem defined in components/pathItems or in an external file.

relationships.description: The path map collects the server base-URL overrides declared on its path items, so that the full set of network locations used by the document's endpoints can be found from this one container.
relationships.evidence: A PathItem listed under 'paths' declares its own 'servers' array whose URLs differ from the root-level servers.

relationships.description: A throttling policy applies across the document's endpoint map as a whole, capping requests to every path the API exposes rather than to one path or method.
relationships.evidence: A vendor extension such as x-rate-limit attached to the paths object, or a gateway configuration that applies a quota to every route imported from the OpenAPI document.

relationships.description: Each path item is an entry owned by the document's path map, keyed by its URL template, and has no place in the API surface outside that container.
relationships.evidence: The OpenAPI document's 'paths' object contains a key such as '/users/{id}' whose value is an inline PathItem object.

relationships.description: The endpoint map points readers to externally hosted documentation that describes the API's resource paths as a whole.
relationships.evidence: An x-externalDocs-style extension on the paths object, or the root externalDocs URL, describes the path structure of the API.

relationships.description: The endpoint map draws on the document's tag labels to group the operations under its paths into categories for documentation and tooling.
relationships.evidence: Operations nested under 'paths' list tag names in their 'tags' field that match entries in the root 'tags' array.

relationships.description: The path map makes each HTTP method-path operation reachable by resolving a request URL to the path item that holds the operation.
relationships.evidence: An operation such as 'get' appears under a path key in 'paths', and a router generated from the document dispatches requests for that path and method to the operation's handler.

notes: Paths aggregates and composes PathItem redundantly; keep composes, using aggregates only for $ref'd components/pathItems. Paths has no servers, externalDocs or tags fields: those belong to PathItem, Operation or root, so those links are transitive at best. 'serves Operation' misstates containment; Operations belong to PathItem.
